Servicios Adicionales del Auditor Externo Aprobados por el Comite de Auditoria

FECHA: 30/10/2026

BOLSA MEXICANA DE VALORES, S.A.B. DE C.V., INFORMA:

CLAVE COTIZACIÓN :

GISSA

RAZÓN SOCIAL :

GRUPO INDUSTRIAL SALTILLO, S.A.B. DE C.V.

RAZÓN SOCIAL DEL AUDITOR EXTERNO :

Galaz, Yamazaki, Ruiz Urquiza, S.C.

DESCRIPCIÓN DE LOS SERVICIOS ADICIONALES APROBADOS POR EL COMITÉ DE AUDITORIA :

AVISO DE LA CONTRATACIÓN DE SERVICIOS ADICIONALES A LOS DE AUDITORIA

Grupo Industrial Saltillo, S.A.B. de C.V. (en lo sucesivo la "Sociedad" o la "Emisora") informa a esa Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores la contratación de servicios adicionales a los servicios de auditoría del Auditor Externo del Despacho Galaz, Yamazaki, Ruiz Urquiza, S.C. (Deloitte) en el que presta sus servicios dicho Auditor Externo (el "Auditor"), consistente en:

  • Elaboración de dictamen del Seguro Social, INFONAVIT y Contribuciones locales, por un monto aproximado de honorarios de $700,000 M.N.

  • Asesoría fiscal en materia de precios de transferencia y Dictamen Fiscal, por un costo aproximado de $3,300,000 M.N.

  • Elaboración de estudio respecto del Estado de Información No Financiera de las empresas de Draxton Global a fin de dar cumplimiento a la normativa correspondiente. El servicio tiene un costo aproximado de $800,000 M.N.

La contratación de los servicios adicionales antes mencionados, fueron autorizados por el Comité de Auditoría el 16 de octubre de 2026 y por el Consejo de Administración de la Sociedad el 20 de octubre de 2026. Dichos servicios equivalen a un monto total de $4,800,000 M.N. contrastado con los honorarios por la auditoría externa de estados financieros básicos anuales que corresponden a un monto total de $18,000,000 M.N. aproximadamente.

La prestación de los servicios adicionales descritos en el presente aviso no afecta la independencia del Auditor, ni del equipo de trabajo de auditores externos, en la prestación a la Sociedad del servicio de auditoría de estados financieros básicos del ejercicio en curso, en virtud de que los servicios adicionales: (i) no se ubican en la lista establecida en el Artículo 6, fracción VII de las Disposiciones de Carácter General Aplicables a las Entidades y Emisoras Supervisadas por la Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores que Contraten Servicios de Auditoría Externa de Estados Financiero Básicos (las "Disposiciones"); (ii) el Auditor y el respectivo equipo de trabajo, no estarán en la posición de auditar su propio trabajo; (iii) no actuarán como parte de la administración o del personal de la Sociedad, ni realizarán actividades cuya responsabilidad recaiga en la administración o el personal de la Sociedad; y (iv) dichos servicios no pondrán al Auditor en la posición de defensor o abogado de la Sociedad y la prestación de los servicios no representará un conflicto de interés entre el Auditor y la Sociedad.

Informamos lo anterior de acuerdo con lo previsto en el artículo 19 de las Disposiciones. Atentamente,

Grupo Industrial Saltillo, S.A.B. de C.V.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Monterrey, México, 30 de octubre 2026 - Arca Continental, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: AC*) ("Arca Continental" o "AC"), el segundo embotellador más grande de Coca-Cola en América Latina, anunció sus resultados para el tercer trimestre de 2026 y acumulado a septiembre 2026 ("3T26" y "9M26").

DATOS RELEVANTES PARA EL TERCER TRIMESTRE DE 2026

  • Ventas Netas incrementaron 5.9% en comparación con el 3T25, registrando Ps. 66,613 millones.

  • EBITDA aumentó 6.2% a Ps. 13,625 millones con un margen de 20.5%.

  • Utilidad Neta fue de Ps. 5,054 millones con un margen de 7.6%.

DATOS RELEVANTES PARA EL ACUMULADO A SEPTIEMBRE 2026

  • Ventas Netas incrementaron 2.1% en comparación con el 9M25, registrando Ps. 187,229 millones.

  • EBITDA aumentó 2.1% comparado con el mismo periodo de 2025 a Ps. 37,388 millones con un margen de 20.0%.

  • Utilidad Neta fue de Ps. 13,798 millones con un margen de 7.4%.

COMENTARIO DEL DIRECTOR GENERAL

"Durante el tercer trimestre de 2026 logramos una mejora significativa en el desempeño de nuestras operaciones, con crecimiento de 4.6% en volumen consolidado y de 6.2% en EBITDA, alcanzando un margen de 20.5%. Estos resultados reflejan la capacidad de nuestro modelo de negocio para adaptarse con velocidad y flexibilidad a las condiciones de cada mercado, fortaleciendo la ejecución comercial y operativa, al tiempo que mantenemos una gestión financiera prudente", señaló Arturo Gutiérrez, Director General de Arca Continental.

"Seguiremos enfocados en fortalecer nuestras capacidades comerciales y digitales, mantenernos cerca de clientes y consumidores y ejecutar con disciplina en cada uno de nuestros mercados, con una visión de largo plazo orientada a generar valor sostenible y contribuir al desarrollo de las comunidades donde operamos", agregó.

Acerca de Arca Continental

"During the third quarter of 2026 we achieved a significant improvement in the performance of our operations, with 4.6% growth in consolidated volume and a 6.2% increase in EBITDA, reaching a margin of 20.5%. These results reflect the capability of our business model to adapt rapidly and with flexibility to the conditions of each market, strengthening our commercial and operational execution, while maintaining prudent financial management", stated Arturo Gutierrez, Chief Executive Officer of Arca Continental.

"We will continue to focus on making our commercial and digital capabilities stronger, remain close to our customers and consumers, and execute with discipline in every one of our markets, with a long-term vision aimed at generating sustainable value and contributing to the development of the communities we serve", he added.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

New York: Fitch Ratings has issued the following commentary:

Fitch Ratings has affirmed the Long-Term Foreign and Local Currency Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) of Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. de C.V. (GFNorte) and Banco Mercantil del Norte, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Banorte) at 'BBB-‌' due to an affirmation of Banorte's Viability Rating (VR) at 'bbb-‌'‌. The Short-Term Foreign and Local Currency IDRs were affirmed at 'F3', and Banorte's Government Support Rating (GSR) was affirmed at 'bb+'. The Rating Outlook for the Long-Term IDRs is Positive.

Fitch has also affirmed the Long- and Short-Term National Scale Ratings of Banorte, Arrendadora y Factor Banorte, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.R., Grupo Financiero Banorte (AyF Banorte), Casa de Bolsa Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Grupo Financiero Banorte (CB Banorte) and Almacenadora Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Organizacion Auxiliar del Credito, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Almacenadora Banorte) at 'AAA(mex)' and 'F1+(mex)', respectively. The Rating Outlook for all the Long-Term National Ratings is Stable. A full list of ratings actions is at the end of this press release.


KEY RATING DRIVERS
Stable Operating Environment: The score for the operating environment (OE) was affirmed at 'bb+' with a stable outlook and is below its implied score of 'bbb'. Operating conditions for Mexican banks remain good, but subdued economic performance continues to influence banks' ability to generate businesses. The country's estimated GDP per capita for 2026 is USD16,234, and Fitch's Operational Risk Index (ORI) percentile was 45.8% in October 2026, supporting the implied OE score of 'bbb'. Fitch adjusted the implied OE score, viewing economic performance as a negative factor.


Positive Outlook: The Positive Rating Outlook reflects the continued improvements in Banorte's overall business and financial profiles. Fitch expects these improvements to be sustained, with an operating profit-to-risk weighted assets (RWA) ratios above 4.75% and a common equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio close to 14%, while reducing gradually its exposure to the public sector. If sustained, these improvements could lead to positive rating action over the next 12 months.


Strong Performance Drives Ratings: Banorte's IDRs and National Ratings are driven by its 'bbb-‌' VR. The VR reflects the bank's consolidated business profile and strong risk framework, as well as good financial performance over the economic cycle. Fitch affirmed Banorte's Business Profile score at 'bbb-‌' with outlook positive. Fitch believes Banorte will continue to consolidate its leading position in Mexico by gaining market share and widening the gap among its followers. Banorte's four-year average total operating income (TOI) from 2022-2025 was USD6.5 billion, gradually exceeding that of its closest peers.


Prudent Risk Management: Fitch affirmed Banorte's risk profile score at 'bbb-‌' with outlook positive. This reflects the bank's sound and consistent underwriting standards across economic cycles, as well as its solid risk-control framework, which Fitch views as aligned with its business profile. Strong capitalization metrics and ample collateral have consistently supported prudent balance-sheet growth. These factors mitigate Banorte's higher concentrations relative to certain peers. Banorte's consistent risk profile, along with a robust risk infrastructure, ensures effective credit quality control and monitoring of various risks. A sustained downward trend in the exposure to the Mexican sovereign would be viewed favorably by Fitch and could support upward momentum in the Risk Profile assessment.


Sound Asset Quality: Banorte's asset quality score of 'bbb-‌' reflects broadly stable metrics over the past five years. Stage 3 loans as a proportion of gross loans were 1.5% in 2Q26 from a four-year average of 1.1%, due to an isolated commercial loan exposure from 3Q25 and the consolidation of the loan portfolio of Tarjetas del Futuro. However, NPL metrics across all credit segments have been stable and compare favorably to peers. Fitch expects the NPL ratio to return to historical levels. Banorte's prudent underwriting standards and high collateral coverage continue to support the 'bbb-‌' asset quality score, which should support recovery prospects.


Strong and Resilient Profitability: Fitch's 'bbb-‌' assessment of Banorte's earnings and profitability reflects its consistent operating profitability, supported by resilient net interest income, moderate credit costs and operating efficiencies. The operating profit-to-RWA ratio was 6.2% in 2Q26, compared with 5.9% on average for 2022-2025. Banorte's profitability metrics compare favorable to peers, and it is one of the most profitable banks among Mexico's largest banks. Fitch expects core profitability metrics to be sustained close to 6%.


Strong Capitalization: Fitch assesses Banorte's capitalization and leverage score at 'bbb-‌'‌, reflecting robust capital metrics and ample buffers above local regulatory requirements. The bank's CET1 ratio was 12.6% in 2Q26, down from 14% in 2Q25 due to dividend payments. Fitch expects the CET1 ratio to recover to 13% or above through the bank's earnings generation. Loss-absorbing hybrid instruments, primarily additional Tier 1 (AT1) securities, supported a total capital ratio of 21.5% on the same date, which Fitch views positively. Fitch expects Banorte's capital to remain sufficient to absorb expected loan growth and support consistent dividend distributions.


Enhanced Funding and Liquidity Profile: Banorte's funding and liquidity factor score of 'bbb-‌' reflects structural improvements in its funding mix and financing costs. The bank's loans-to-deposits ratio was 103.5% in 2Q26, compared with a 2022-2025 average of 102.0%. Its net stable funding ratio was 132% in 2Q26. Increasing demand for deposits is a key component of Banorte's funding strategy; these represented 67.4% of total customer deposits in 2Q26 and are trending toward peer levels.


RATING SENSITIVITIES
Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade
--The Outlook could be revised to Stable if Banorte is not able to sustain the improvements in its business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's VRs and IDRs are sensitive to a rating action on Mexico's sovereign ratings or a downward revision of Fitch's OE assessment.

--Banorte's ratings could be downgraded if financial performance deteriorates consistently, with the operating profit-to-RWA ratio falling below 2.5%, the CET1-to-RWA ratio decreasing below 12% or a weakening of Fitch's risk profile assessment, denoting asset quality deterioration.

--A significant increase in the bank's exposure to the sovereign may also trigger a VR downgrade to the same level of the sovereign rating.

--Banorte's national scale ratings will reflect any change in local relativities.


Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade
--The VR and IDRs could be upgraded if the sovereign rating is upgraded and Fitch revises upward its OE assessment, while the bank maintains very strong business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's ratings could be upgraded if TOI growth continues, financial performance remains solid and consistent, an operating profit-to-RWA ratio above 4.75%, a CET1-to-RWA and total capital ratios close or above 14% and 21%, respectively, asset quality metrics remain at reasonable levels, and Mexican sovereign exposure declines, considering a sovereign debt to CET1 ratio at or below 2x.

--Banorte's national scale ratings cannot be upgraded because they are at the highest level on the national ratings scale.


OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: KEY RATING DRIVERS
Banorte's Senior Unsecured Debt: The local senior unsecured debt ratings are at the same level as Banorte's 'AAA(mex)' National Long-Term Rating, as the notes' likelihood of default is the same as that of the issuer and average expected recoveries.

Banorte Classified as D-SIB: Banorte's 'bb+' GSR reflects its high systemic importance. The bank is defined as a domestic systemically important bank (D-SIB). Fitch considers the authorities' propensity to support as high given its market share and ample interconnectivity within the financial system, to avoid contagion risks.

As of 2Q26, Banorte's market share in customer deposits was 14.0%, ranking as the second-largest bank in the system. However, Fitch believes the likelihood of support for Banorte is lower than other large policy banks due to Banorte's private ownership.


OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: RATING SENSITIVITIES
Debt Ratings

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's senior debt rating would mirror any downgrade in the issuer's national scale ratings.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--Banorte's senior debt rating has no improvement potential because it is at the highest level on the national rating scale.

Government Support Rating

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's GSR could occur if the sovereign's ability to support the bank is weakened by a sovereign rating downgrade, or if the sovereign's propensity to support the bank becomes less likely.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--An upgrade to Banorte's GSR is possible in the event of a sovereign upgrade coinciding with a strengthening of the sovereign's ability and propensity to support the bank.


SUBSIDIARIES & AFFILIATES: KEY RATING DRIVERS
GFNorte's Ratings Equalized with Banorte's: Fitch considers GFNorte's failure risk to be substantially the same as that of Banorte, given GFNorte's reliance on dividend flows from, and the value of, its investment in the bank. GFNorte's ratings also reflect its low double-leverage ratio, a highly relevant factor measured as investments in subsidiaries relative to tangible equity.

The double-leverage ratio was 98.2% at 2Q26, compared with 96.4% at 2Q25, and remained well below Fitch's 120% threshold.

Support Underpins Subsidiaries' National Ratings: The National Ratings of CB Banorte, AyF Banorte and Almacenadora Banorte reflect the credit profile of their holding company, GFNorte, which is driven by Banorte, the group's main operating entity. Fitch factors in the explicit support that the financial group would provide to these entities, given their roles in the group's business-diversification strategy and GFNorte's legal obligation to support its subsidiaries.


SUBSIDIARIES AND AFFILIATES: RATING SENSITIVITIES
Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--GFNorte's IDRs could be downgraded if there is a significant and sustained increase in double leverage above 120%. This would lead to one level below Banorte' IDRs.

--Any negative movement in the ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries would be driven by a negative action on Banorte's national ratings.

--A change in the strategic importance of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries to the group and the bank could negatively affect their ratings.

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--An upgrade of GFNorte's IDRs would result from any positive change in Banorte's VR.

--The ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries are at the highest level on the national scale; therefore, there is no possibility of an upgrade to these ratings.


VR ADJUSTMENTS
The operating environment score of 'bb+' is below the 'bbb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): economic performance (negative).

The asset quality score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): collateral and reserves (positive).

The capitalization & leverage score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): leverage and risk-weight calculation (positive).

The funding & liquidity score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): deposit structure (positive).


SUMMARY OF FINANCIAL ADJUSTMENTS
Fitch's tangible capital calculation excluded prepaid expenses and other deferred assets from shareholders' equity.


REFERENCES FOR SUBSTANTIALLY MATERIAL SOURCE CITED AS KEY DRIVER OF RATING
The principal sources of information used in the analysis are described in the Applicable Criteria.

PUBLIC RATINGS WITH CREDIT LINKAGE TO OTHER RATINGS
GFNorte's IDRs and Almacenadora Banorte, AyF Banorte, Casa de Bolsa Banorte's ratings and Outlook are linked with those of Banorte.


ESG CONSIDERATIONS
The highest level of ESG credit relevance is a score of '3', unless otherwise disclosed in this section. A score of '3' means ESG issues are credit-neutral or have only a minimal credit impact on the entity, either due to their nature or the way in which they are being managed by the entity. Fitch's ESG Relevance Scores are not inputs in the rating process; they are an observation on the relevance and materiality of ESG factors in the rating decision. For more information on Fitch's ESG Relevance Scores, visit https://www.fitchratings.com/topics/esg/products#esg-relevance-scores.

Support Underpins Subsidiaries' National Ratings: The National Ratings of CB Banorte, AyF Banorte and Almacenadora Banorte reflect the credit profile of their holding company, GFNorte, which is driven by Banorte, the group's main operating entity. Fitch factors in the explicit support that the financial group would provide to these entities, given their roles in the group's business-diversification strategy and GFNorte's legal obligation to support its subsidiaries.

SUBSIDIARIES AND AFFILIATES: RATING SENSITIVITIES
Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--GFNorte's IDRs could be downgraded if there is a significant and sustained increase in double leverage above 120%. This would lead to one level below Banorte' IDRs.

--Any negative movement in the ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries would be driven by a negative action on Banorte's national ratings.

--A change in the strategic importance of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries to the group and the bank could negatively affect their ratings.

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--An upgrade of GFNorte's IDRs would result from any positive change in Banorte's VR.

--The ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries are at the highest level on the national scale; therefore, there is no possibility of an upgrade to these ratings.

The asset quality score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): collateral and reserves (positive).

The capitalization & leverage score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): leverage and risk-weight calculation (positive).

The funding & liquidity score of 'bbb-‌' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): deposit structure (positive).

SUMMARY OF FINANCIAL ADJUSTMENTS
Fitch's tangible capital calculation excluded prepaid expenses and other deferred assets from shareholders' equity.

REFERENCES FOR SUBSTANTIALLY MATERIAL SOURCE CITED AS KEY DRIVER OF RATING
The principal sources of information used in the analysis are described in the Applicable Criteria.

PUBLIC RATINGS WITH CREDIT LINKAGE TO OTHER RATINGS

ESG CONSIDERATIONS
The highest level of ESG credit relevance is a score of '3', unless otherwise disclosed in this section. A score of '3' means ESG issues are credit-neutral or have only a minimal credit impact on the entity, either due to their nature or the way in which they are being managed by the entity. CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 30 oct (Reuters) - La bolsa mexicana caía en sus primeras operaciones del viernes, en la última sesión de la temporada local de resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre, pero se encaminaba a cerrar octubre con un sólido desempeño mensual.

El índice S&P/BMV IPC .MXX bajaba un 0.60% a 69,365.97 puntos, presionado principalmente por firmas del sector minero. Pese al declive, la bolsa acumulaba en octubre un retorno del 8%, su mejor desempeño mensual desde noviembre de 2023.

Las acciones de Grupo México GMEXICOB.MX, uno de los principales productores de cobre del mundo, encabezaban las pérdidas de la jornada, con una caída de un 2.53% a 227.76 pesos.

Eran seguidos por los títulos de Industrias Peñoles PEOLES.MX, el mayor productor mundial de plata, que restaban un 2.20% a 772.05 pesos.

(Reporte de Noé Torres)

(( noe.torres@thomsonreuters.com ;))

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

Gonçalo Regalado, CEO of Banco Português de Fomento, remarked during the launch of the SME Bonds that the bank views this new product as essential for small and medium enterprises to find financing alternatives beyond traditional bank credit. Moreover, because it was designed from the outset for such companies, it possesses the necessary and sufficient level of sophistication while also offering compliance guarantees with the most rigorous risk analysis practices.

Alberto Amaral, CEO of Raize, stated at the second of two roundtables presenting the SME Bonds that the preference of SMEs for bank credit when seeking funding is "cultural." This is the case for more than 80% of companies, but it doesn't have to be that way; in the United States, he noted, this figure does not exceed 50%. Therefore, the market is "above all waiting for innovation" that allows them to access capital in diverse and competitive ways. Additionally, the product caters to "investors who want to place their capital in the real economy."

In this context, "the product makes sense, it's a true alternative" and increases, among entrepreneurs, their "ability to make decisions without being dependent on traditional solutions."

Participating in the debate, Rui Veloso, head of Turismo de Portugal and also involved with the new product, noted that the SME Bonds fulfill "a strategy for diversification and providing various financing means to the sector."

Working "in a partnership approach" with IAPMEI and CMVM, Turismo de Portugal has long sought ways to bring companies from the sector into the market. The first time this was considered was in 2018, when they asked, "Why not bonds?" The answer was a positive response to that logic. It was important to create something ambitious "but with pragmatism" that addressed a clearly identified market gap (the lack of alternatives) recognized by Turismo de Portugal. There will certainly be no shortage of market: the companies that are already under the umbrella of the 360 program.

Indeed, the Turismo 360º Enterprises Program is a government initiative based on public funding, developed by Turismo de Portugal in partnership with various entities — including BPF — aimed at accelerating the tourism sector's transition to sustainability and ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) practices. In Rui Veloso's view, the program can serve as a true breeding ground for growing interest in the SME Bonds.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV (ASUR), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages and develops a network of airports primarily in the southeastern region, including key hubs like Cancun International Airport. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail, advertising, and real estate development within airport facilities. ASUR has experienced robust growth in international passenger traffic, driven by the surge in tourism to popular destinations like Cancun and the Riviera Maya, which has become one of its fastest-expanding segments. Additionally, commercial revenue streams from airport concessions and enhanced infrastructure projects, such as terminal expansions and digital services, have fueled this momentum. Operating under a concession model, ASUR focuses on efficiency and sustainability to capitalize on Mexico's rising air travel demand, positioning the company as a vital player in the country's aviation sector. It is Mexico's 2nd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Promotora Y Operadora De Infraestructura, S.A.B. De C.V. (PINFRA), a leading Mexican infrastructure company listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, specializes in the development, construction, operation, and maintenance of transportation and infrastructure assets. Its core activities encompass toll roads, bridges, airports, and railways, primarily through public-private concessions that generate revenue via user fees and long-term contracts. The company plays a vital role in Mexico's economic growth by enhancing connectivity and mobility across key regions. Among its fastest-growing segments are airport operations, which have expanded significantly due to increasing passenger traffic and new terminal developments, as well as concessions for modern toll highways that benefit from rising vehicular demand and government infrastructure initiatives. PINFRA's strategic focus on sustainable projects and operational efficiency has positioned it as a key player in the sector, contributing to national development while delivering consistent returns for shareholders. It is Mexico's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

However, a strong peso negatively impacted Femsa's overseas earnings, particularly affecting its European convenience store business, Valora. "As we approach the last quarter of the year, we remain mindful that the consumption environment in Mexico continues to be weak, Brazil has faced some volatility recently, and we will encounter a more challenging comparison base in the upcoming quarters." Total revenues from Oxxo Mexico rose 10.3% compared to the same quarter last year, while operating profit increased by 5.8%. Femsa stated that its consolidated net profit reached 10.57 billion pesos, an 81% increase compared to the third quarter of 2025.

Megacable reported positive financial results in the third quarter of 2026 and reaffirmed its strategy to focus on operational efficiencies to strengthen the company's profitability. The Guadalajara-based company reported an EBITDA of 4.326 billion pesos, which represents a 10% increase compared to 3.945 billion pesos earned in the same period last year.

Megacable Strengthens as a Fixed Services Provider

The company explained that the positive performance was associated with a moderation in service costs, which only rose by 2.3% compared to the same quarter of the previous year. Additionally, expenses increased by 5.8%, below the rise in revenues. The dynamics of operational efficiency and lower operational spending boosted the company's net profit, which reached 813 million pesos during the period, marking a 30% year-over-year increase. "This performance reflects the company's operational discipline and its focus on more efficient resource management following a phase of expansion and investment in infrastructure," the company, led by Enrique Yamuni, stated in its financial report. In the last quarter of 2021, Megacable announced a 2 billion dollar investment to grow its fiber-optic network and expand its national presence in new markets. The company is currently in the final stages of its five-year plan, paving the way for the consolidation of its position in the fixed internet market, and is even considering the acquisition of other players in the sector, although it has yet to determine whether the operation will be with a fixed or mobile operator.

Megacable is on the verge of surpassing Televisa as the second-largest operator by market share after nearly a decade of Televisa holding that position. This strategy is already reflected in its sales and user numbers. From July to September, revenues rose to 9.504 billion pesos, representing a 7% annual increase. Meanwhile, the total for the first nine months reached 28.191 billion pesos, also a 7% increase. The performance is attributed to an expansion in its subscriber base, particularly in internet services, and the stabilization of the churn rate. During this period, Megacable added 60,000 and 84,000 subscribers in its internet and fixed-line telephony segments, respectively. This figure indicates a 6% increase compared to the additions reported during the same period in 2025.

However, the focus on profitability and the conclusion of its expansion phase have been reflected in a reduction in investments. During the third quarter, Megacable allocated 2.372 billion pesos to this area, equivalent to 25% of its revenues. Although this period typically sees a higher level of investment due to seasonality, the company acknowledged that this is the lowest amount for a third quarter since it began its expansion phase. Megacable's financial results demonstrate a business that is advancing toward consolidation in the fixed telecommunications market, one of the most competitive in the industry. However, the landscape may change with Televisa's acquisition of AT&T Mexico, an operation that, according to analysts, could accelerate commercial adjustments and investment decisions among competitors in the sector, including Megacable.

The company explained that the positive performance was associated with a moderation in service costs, which only rose by 2.3% compared to the same quarter of the previous year. Additionally, expenses increased by 5.8%, below the rise in revenues. The dynamics of operational efficiency and lower operational spending boosted the company's net profit, which reached 813 million pesos during the period, marking a 30% year-over-year increase. "This performance reflects the company's operational discipline and its focus on more efficient resource management following a phase of expansion and investment in infrastructure," the company, led by Enrique Yamuni, stated in its financial report. In the last quarter of 2021, Megacable announced a 2 billion dollar investment to grow its fiber-optic network and expand its national presence in new markets. The company is currently in the final stages of its five-year plan, paving the way for the consolidation of its position in the fixed internet market, and is even considering the acquisition of other players in the sector, although it has yet to determine whether the operation will be with a fixed or mobile operator.

Megacable is on the verge of surpassing Televisa as the second-largest operator by market share after nearly a decade of Televisa holding that position. This strategy is already reflected in its sales and user numbers. From July to September, revenues rose to 9.504 billion pesos, representing a 7% annual increase. Meanwhile, the total for the first nine months reached 28.191 billion pesos, also a 7% increase. The performance is attributed to an expansion in its subscriber base, particularly in internet services, and the stabilization of the churn rate. During this period, Megacable added 60,000 and 84,000 subscribers in its internet and fixed-line telephony segments, respectively. This figure indicates a 6% increase compared to the additions reported during the same period in 2025.

However, the focus on profitability and the conclusion of its expansion phase have been reflected in a reduction in investments. During the third quarter, Megacable allocated 2.372 billion pesos to this area, equivalent to 25% of its revenues. Although this period typically sees a higher level of investment due to seasonality, the company acknowledged that this is the lowest amount for a third quarter since it began its expansion phase. Megacable's financial results demonstrate a business that is advancing toward consolidation in the fixed telecommunications market, one of the most competitive in the industry. However, the landscape may change with Televisa's acquisition of AT&T Mexico, an operation that, according to analysts, could accelerate commercial adjustments and investment decisions among competitors in the sector, including Megacable.

Megacable, a Mexican telecommunications operator, reported an increase in its revenues and operating cash flow during the third quarter, despite a lower level of investment.

The company's revenues grew by 7% compared to the same period last year, driven by the expansion of its internet subscriber base and the stabilization of its disconnection rate. Sales were 0.2% below the forecasts set by the consensus gathered by Infosel.

Meanwhile, operating cash flow rose by 10% thanks to a strategy focused on profitability, exceeding market estimates by 1.8%.

"The company achieved the highest EBITDA (operating cash flow) level in its history and managed a margin expansion of 130 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025," the company highlighted in its statement.

Megacable, which has reduced its investment levels to 25% of its revenue, recorded a 25% increase in its cash flow, totaling 1,954 million pesos. This larger available cash flow, linked to operational growth, allowed it to reduce net debt by 8.8%.

Additionally, the leverage ratio decreased from 1.45 times, recorded in the third quarter of 2025, to 1.21x, "remaining within the ranges established by the company."

Finally, the net profit for the period increased by 30% due to lower financial expenses, although it was 2.1% below consensus expectations.

October 29 (Axis Negocios) -- Banco del Bajío, a lender focused on businesses, has lowered its earnings forecast for the entire year of 2026 after missing expectations for three consecutive quarters.

The financial institution's forecast decreased from a range between 8.4 billion and 9 billion pesos to 8 billion pesos. Compared to the previous year's performance, the July estimate implied a drop of between 0.6% and 7.3%, while the current estimate indicates an expected decline of 11.7%.

"As a result [of flat commissions and intermediation income], and considering the high provisions recognized in this quarter, we currently foresee that net income will be around 8 billion pesos, and that return on average equity will be approximately 16% for the fiscal year," said Carlos de la Cerda, the company's executive vice president, during the third-quarter results conference.

BanBajío, as the institution is commonly known, reported its lowest earnings in 18 quarters for the third quarter of the year, marking a 21.3% decline compared to the previous year, which signifies the ninth consecutive disappointment for analysts' expectations.

Following this, the bank's earnings recorded a 14.2% drop in the current year, making a revision of its annual guidance predictable. Thus, 2026 will become the third consecutive year of lower profits for the institution, a situation unprecedented in over 20 years of public records.

Amid this scenario, the lender's management aimed to convey a message of confidence, anticipating clear improvements for 2027.

"The strong portfolio growth we are generating today should increasingly translate into revenue growth through net interest margin, fees, effects, and trading, with disciplined expenses and normalized risk costs. The key drivers for profit growth are already in place," De la Cerda pointed out.

BanBajío aims to increase its earnings per share at a double-digit rate in 2027, and in that year, its return on equity (ROE) is expected to reach between 17% and 18%.

Growth Without Deterioration of Assets

The lender also insisted that its expansion has been continuous and even stated that it plans to exceed its growth guidance for the portfolio of between 11% and 12%, which had been revised from an original proposal of between 8% and 10%.

The issuer, which has seen a portfolio increase of 16.5% up to September, indicated that its goal is to continue growing over the next few years at a pace of 1.2 times that of the banking system. This will allow it to consistently gain market share.

"Among the 10 largest banks in corporate credit, we gained the largest market share in the first eight months of the year," said Joaquín Domínguez, the company's chief financial officer. "We continue to believe that strong growth and disciplined asset quality can coexist."

In light of the prospects, analysts questioned the quality of the assets, to which BanBajío responded, without providing specific estimates, that it plans to maintain its delinquency and risk cost below those of the sector.

As of the end of September, the financial institution's delinquency rate was 1.8%, compared to 2.3% for the banking system; while its risk cost reached 1.2%, compared to 3.5% for all lenders combined.

"The growth we are achieving in the market has not changed our risk acceptance criteria, so we remain very consistent with the assets we are acquiring," insisted the CFO.

BanBajío even anticipated that it sees significant opportunities in specific business sectors, such as manufacturing related to artificial intelligence and data centers; the real estate sector, particularly in logistics; and the energy sector.

Additionally, it stated that there is ample room to provide financing in the small and medium-sized enterprise market, although the company would not target the segment of the smallest businesses.

Reaction

For some, BanBajío's outlook did represent a counterbalance to the unfavorable numbers.

"Despite a quarterly performance weaker than expected, the management's moderate projections for 2027 lead us to maintain a positive view on BanBajío," wrote analysts from GBM Casa de Bolsa in a report.

The specialists highlighted the portfolio growth, increased market share, and stabilization of margins as indicators of potential profitability recovery.

The company's shares fell 2.7% on a day when the main market index, the S&P/BMV IPC, gained 0.7%. Earlier in the session, the stock had dropped by 4%.

Despite the decline, BanBajío has gained 22% so far in 2026, nearly tripling the 7.8% rise of the most representative stock basket.

Additionally, it stated that there is ample room to provide financing in the small and medium-sized enterprise market, although the company would not target the segment of the smallest businesses.

Reaction

For some, BanBajío's outlook did represent a counterbalance to the unfavorable numbers.

"Despite a quarterly performance weaker than expected, the management's moderate projections for 2027 lead us to maintain a positive view on BanBajío," wrote analysts from GBM Casa de Bolsa in a report.

The specialists highlighted the portfolio growth, increased market share, and stabilization of margins as indicators of potential profitability recovery.

The company's shares fell 2.7% on a day when the main market index, the S&P/BMV IPC, gained 0.7%. Earlier in the session, the stock had dropped by 4%.

Despite the decline, BanBajío has gained 22% so far in 2026, nearly tripling the 7.8% rise of the most representative stock basket.

• EU enters winter with gas storage 75% full versus 83% a year earlier
  • European gas prices briefly touch €100/MWh for first time since December 2022
  • Commission starts dialogue with oil refineries to boost production

By Julia Payne

BRUSSELS, Oct 29 (Reuters) - EU energy ministers will meet on Thursday to discuss energy security ahead of the winter heating season as the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Yemen send oil and natural gas prices soaring.

Fighting has damaged refineries across the Middle East and Russia, and hampered oil and gas flows through vital shipping lanes in the Black Sea, Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz.

"We are in a very serious situation now. It does not look like we have a security of supply issue but I would warn against neglecting that," EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen told reporters on Wednesday. He said affordability was just as urgent an issue, arguing that available supply meant little to households and businesses that could not afford it.

The Commission began talks with European refineries on Wednesday to find ways to boost output, including through the possible easing of some technical specifications.

Western powers also agreed this month to accelerate the release of over 400 million barrels of emergency oil stocks after US pressure.

EU countries will also discuss a Commission proposal to cut electricity bills through tax and grid fee reforms, such as by taxing electricity at a lower rate than natural gas.

The EU is entering the winter heating season, with stocks at only 75% of available storage , versus 83% a year ago.

European wholesale gas prices briefly touched €100/MWh on Wednesday for the first time since December 2022 when Europe was reeling from the loss of most of its Russian pipeline gas supply. Prices have been rising as the conflict in the Middle East escalated, and are now trading at around triple pre-Iran war levels.

(Reporting by Julia Payne
Editing by Keith Weir)

(( julia.payne@thomsonreuters.com ;))

Reports Outline Biological Factors Study Results from Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences (Preparation, Characterization, and Inhibitory Activity of Bacillus velezensis Crude Protein-based Composite Film Against the Fungal Pathogen of ...)

2026 OCT 28-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at NewsRx Drug Daily-- Research findings on biological factors are discussed in a new report. According to news originating from Nanning, People' s Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated," To develop a new biodegradable antifungal packaging material, this study employed a casting method to... 2026 OCT 28 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at NewsRx Drug Daily -- Research findings on biological factors are discussed in a new report. According to news originating from Nanning, People's Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated, "To develop a new biodegradable antifungal packaging material, this study employed a casting method to prepare composite films using carboxymethyl chitosan and konjac glucomannan as film forming materials, with the incorporating varying proportions of crude protein extract from Bacillus velezensis T9."

Our news editors obtained a quote from the research from Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences: "The morphology and chemical structure of the composite films were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The physical, chemical, antifungal and preservation properties of the composite films were investigated. The results showed that the introduction of T9 crude protein increased the roughness and thickness of the composite films, but reduced its tensile strength, water vapor transmission rate, and light transmittance (P<0.05). All composite films exhibited good environmental biodegradability, with biodegradation rates exceeding 90% within 20 days. With increasing concentrations of T9 crude protein, the composite films demonstrated significantly enhanced antifungal activity against Apiospora arundinis (A. arundinis) and a markedly increased inhibition rate on 3-nitropropionic acid (3-NPA) mycotoxin synthesis (P<0.05). When the T9 crude protein addition reached 0.12% (KCB12 treatment), the inhibition zone diameter against A. arundinis reached 20.5 mm, the lesion length on sugarcane decreased by 51.03%~65.09% compared to the control group (CK), and no 3-NPA toxin was detected."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "Furthermore, KCB12 treatment significantly reduced the weight loss rate (P<0.05), delayed the decrease in sugarcane juice pH, and maintained higher levels of soluble solids and sucrose content in sugarcane during storage. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the practical application of crude protein-based composite films from Bacillus velezensis T9 to control mycotoxin contamination and preserve the postharvest quality of sugarcane."

For more information on this research see: Preparation, Characterization, and Inhibitory Activity of Bacillus velezensis Crude Protein-based Composite Film Against the Fungal Pathogen of Moldy Sugarcane. Shipin gongye ke-ji , 2026,47(20):336-346. The publisher for Shipin gongye ke-ji is The editorial department of Science and Technology of Food Industry.

A free version of this journal article is available at https://doi.org/10.13386/j.issn1002-0306.2025090155 .

Our news journalists report that additional information may be obtained by contacting Wenyan JIANG, Agro-products Quality Safety and Testing Technology Research Institute, Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Nanning 530007, People's Republic of China. Additional authors for this research include Xuelian LIANG, Huiling LI, Tianshun WANG, Wei CHEN, Haijun WANG, Weifan LU, Yuning WEI, Qifeng ZHOU, Jie LIAO.

(Our reports deliver fact-based news of research and discoveries from around the world.)

Oct 29 (Reuters) - Google parent Alphabet's results could spark a rocky ride for Asian markets after a subdued offshore session on Wednesday, with the Federal Reserve holding interest rates steady as widely expected.

AI-spending concerns are likely to be revived as Alphabet shares fell 10% in extended trading after the company missed Wall Street profit and revenue expectations while its negative free cash flow reached $9.07 billion, confounding analysts' expectations it would nearly break even. Nasdaq futures are down 1.1% early on Thursday.

The regional data schedule is light. Results from South Korean chipmaker Samsung and a 2.6% after-hours rise in Microsoft shares on forecast-beating results may offer some respite from AI-spending fears.

The Fed left rates steady at 3.75%-4.00%, upgraded its assessment of the economy and acknowledged inflation remained elevated, while signalling it would await further data before making a decision in December. The probability of a rate hike in December rose to 82% from 75% on Tuesday.

US crude futures closed 2% higher on concerns over supply disruptions following an attack on a Saudi Arabia refinery and worries about a flare-up in the Middle East conflict following next week's US midterm elections. The prospect of Benjamin Netanyahu remaining Israel's caretaker prime minister after an inconclusive Israeli election also supported prices.

Dow +0.19%, S&P 500 +0.28%, Nasdaq +0.27% on the steady Fed. Treasury yields bear-steepened on inflation concerns; 2yr unchanged at 4.735%, 10yr +5bps to 5.045% and 30 yr +6.1bps to 5.361%.

The U.S. dollar index =USDshed 0.2%; EUR +0.3%, JPY and CHF +0.1%, GBP +0.15% with the UK budget taken in stride, CNH steady, AUD +0.4% on hawkish comments from the Reserve Bank of Australia, CAD +0.4% after the Bank of Canada raised rates by 25 basis points but NZD -1% after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand unexpectedly held rates. Bitcoin +0.5%.

Gold +0.2% and copper +0.3% on the steady Fed.

For more click on FXBUZ

(Krishna Kumar is a Reuters market analyst. The views expressed are his own. Editing by Sonali Desai)

(( krishna.k@thomsonreuters.com ))

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 05, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces preliminary terminal passenger traffic figures for May 2026, compared with May 2025.

Durante la conferencia de resultados del tercer trimestre, la dirección de Femsa anunció la compra de la participación restante en la empresa de cafeterías, lo que permitirá generar eficiencias en los gastos corporativos, alinear incentivos operativos y fortalecer la propuesta de valor en las tiendas. El CEO de Femsa, José Antonio Fernández Garza, destacó la competencia con otros jugadores que deben pagar regalías de franquicia, y reafirmó su intención de seguir abriendo locales de café de autoservicio. Aunque no se revelaron los términos financieros de la transacción, Femsa ha ido aumentando su participación en Caffenio desde 2012. Caffenio opera alrededor de 300 puntos de venta de autoservicio, que han ganado popularidad entre los consumidores. Además, se enfatizó que este formato independiente servirá como un laboratorio de desarrollo de productos, impulsando la innovación en bebidas de café y alimentos para Oxxo en México y Sudamérica.

India, Oct. 29 -- Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and fled the country. In a circuitous journey, Bolsonaro left for Argentina on Tuesday with his wife and two daughters, then travelled to Ecuador, according to Argentina officials and flight data. The 45-year-old senator, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, visited the White House in May, and the Trump administration approved US visas for him and his family this week. Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court, accused of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. The court had ordered him to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by Tuesday.P10 Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from HT Pune. MEXICAN STOCK REPORT

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Arca Continental

Debt to Equity Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.36; a deterioration from 0.28 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.20; a deterioration from 0.17 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Altman-Z score of Arca Continental

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Arca Continental with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Arca Continental scores a Z = 0.95 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; an improvement from 0.95 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a deterioration from 0.96 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Liquidity of Arca Continental

Acid Test Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.88; a deterioration from 1.04 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 1.2 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. This change in current ratio was driven by

- A decrease in current assets of MX$9.7 billion (or 13.1%) from the previous quarter and MX$3.3 billion (or 4.8%) from year ago to MX$64.4 billion.

- A decrease in current liabilities of MX$1.4 billion (or 2.5%) from the previous quarter and an increase of MX$11 billion (or 24.1%) from year ago to MX$56.4 billion.

Piotroski F-Score of Arca Continental

Arca Continental has achieved a high Piotroski F-Score of 7 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating solid financial health and operational efficiency. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Arca Continental is not only generating solid earnings and cash flow but also managing its balance sheet prudently positioning it well for sustained growth and investor confidence.

Free Cash Flow (FCF) of Arca Continental

Free Cash Flow (FCF) growth is a fundamental risk metric that reflects a company's capacity to generate surplus cash from its core operations after capital expenditures. This metric directly influences a firm's liquidity, self-sufficiency, and ability to manage obligations without external funding.

A positive and rising FCF generally implies operational efficiency, strong margins, and disciplined investment - all of which reduce financial risk. However, declining or negative FCF growth, particularly over consecutive quarters, may indicate emerging liquidity stress, unsustainable capital outlays, or revenue compression. Monitoring FCF growth helps assess a company's financial flexibility, its vulnerability to external shocks, and the likelihood of financing constraints.

Arca Continental Free Cash Flow for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is MX$8.2 billion; representing a 144.26% increase from MX$3.4 billion in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a 30.12% decrease compared to MX$11.7 billion in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].
